Bluesky events recorded from Jetstream by ClickHouse for JSONBench (github.com/ClickHouse/JSONBench): file_0001.json.gz, 1,000,000 lines, 480,778,277 bytes decoded. time_us is 16 digits, so it types as Int64 and every row is stored at its arrival time, in file order, which is time_us order

JSONBench's 100m dataset: Bluesky events recorded from Jetstream by ClickHouse (github.com/ClickHouse/JSONBench), file_0001 to file_0100.json.gz, 13,372,936,569 bytes to download and 47,813,179,260 decoded by their gzip trailers, about 100,000,000 lines. time_us is 16 digits, so it types as Int64 and every row is stored at its arrival time, as in bluesky-1m

Quickwit's HDFS logs with tenant ids, the dataset of its tutorial "Index a logging dataset locally" (quickwit.io/docs/get-started/tutorials/tutorial-hdfs-logs). Quickwit does not state where the logs come from. hdfs-logs-multitenants.json.gz: 470,061,890 bytes, sha256 673c1b681089fb7ce78745f520a0837fcffce64651b6c4cdc8d1fd3e82a42e08, 20,000,000 lines, 7,194,479,974 bytes decoded, over 393 UTC days from 2015-08-27 to 2016-10-22. Given as `urls`, so it is decoded as it arrives and retried
